name: Algeria

findings.controller: Haut-Commissariat à la Numérisation (High Commission for Digitisation)
findings.summary: The Council of Ministers approved a direct-negotiation contract with Huawei to build a national digital-services data centre for the High Commission for Digitisation; the agreement with a Huawei consortium was signed in Algiers in April 2024. Value undisclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole domestic because the state body owns and operates the centre; Huawei is recorded as builder. If Huawei also supplies the IT equipment, cloud stack or operations (likely for a Huawei-consortium turnkey build, but not stated in the sources), the equipment would be a prc-controlled finding. Both opened sources are one outlet; Radio Algérie page was rejected on fetch.

findings.summary: Ooredoo Group signed a partnership agreement with Huawei to modernise its core network towards 5.5G in several markets, named as including Algeria and Tunisia. No value or binding terms disclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Both reports trace to a Qatar News Agency release (Qatari state agency, S4), so they are not independent of each other. Coded tier 2 because only a partnership agreement is described. Pole is the core-network vendor's (Huawei), not the Qatari operator's.

findings.summary: Mobilis ran a 5G test in Oran with Huawei as technical partner; Mobilis said it planned further tests with ZTE and Ericsson. No supply contract was reported.
findings.analyst_inference: A pilot only. Mobilis's commercial 5G (launched December 2025) vendor is not identified in any source this run opened; an April 2025 Mobilis test report named no vendor. still_current null: the vendor of the live network was not confirmed.

findings.summary: Algérie Télécom awarded Huawei a commercial agreement to deploy a very-high-speed fixed network for one million customers within a year; separately ZTE won a fibre-network contract with a national young-entrepreneurs federation.
findings.analyst_inference: Pre-2020; whether Huawei still supplies and maintains the Algérie Télécom access network was not confirmed, so still_current is null. Value not disclosed.

findings.summary: A 2019 Wall Street Journal investigation, reported by TSA, said Huawei supported Algerian surveillance systems presented as a model to other African states; an Open Technology Fund report cited Huawei safe-city, facial-recognition and censorship technology. Huawei denied the allegations.
findings.analyst_inference: Secondary reporting of investigative claims; no procurement record, location, date of award or value found. Tier 3 is a conservative placeholder for a reportedly deployed system. Same outlet for both sources. Pre-2020 and still_current unconfirmed. A Russian vendor (SpeechPro) was also named, not coded.

findings.controller: Alcatel Submarine Networks (named project partner; vendor role unconfirmed)
findings.summary: The ORVAL/ALVAL submarine cable linking Algiers and Oran to Valencia, Spain, went into service as Algérie Télécom-run infrastructure, with IslaLink and ASN named as project partners.
findings.analyst_inference: Capacity names ASN only as a partner, not explicitly as supplier; pole third (French vendor) is an inference. Date from the Algérie Eco headline seen in search only. Not PRC-built on available evidence.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research
findings.summary: Algeria adopted an inter-ministerial roadmap to implement its national AI strategy, prioritising sovereign open-source models for public services, national high-performance computing and domestic data storage. No model, base weights or vendor named.
findings.analyst_inference: A policy statement (tier 1), not a deployed model. Base model unknown, so base_model and base_model_pole are null. Corroborated as a statement having been made, not as anything built.

silicon.null_reason: no confirmed accelerator purchase or licence found; an April 2026 Huawei-ministry discussion of AI GPU acquisition was reported only by an outlet of unclear standing (algeriatech.news) and not coded

power.null_reason: no AI- or data-centre-specific power evidence surfaced; budget spent on networks and facilities

research_gaps: Which vendors supply RAN and core for Mobilis, Djezzy and Ooredoo commercial 5G (licences December 2025, about US$492m)? No source opened named them.
Does Huawei supply the IT equipment, cloud stack or operations of the High Commission for Digitisation data centre (2024 contract)? Contract value and status?
April 2026 Ministry of Knowledge Economy - Huawei talks on AI GPU acquisition (reported via AL24 News / algeriatech.news): find a primary or S2 source; are Ascend accelerators involved?
Medex branch cable (about US$32m) vendor: the Capacity link redirected; not resolved.
Algerian safe-city / surveillance deployments: any procurement record (Huawei, Hikvision, Dahua, ZTE) and whether still in service.
Sonatrach - Huawei MoU (June 2024) seen in search results only; scope not checked.
WAICO founding membership rests on an S5 roster in the global layer; needs an S1-S3 confirmation.
